title: Timed visual contract
description: What a narration passage obliges the picture to do. Written BEFORE any media is retrieved and before any template is considered. A contract never names a file, a template, or a scene.

sectionPurpose.description: What this section of the documentary is for. Supplied, not inferred per passage.

text.description: Exact narration text for this unit. Verbatim, never paraphrased.

wordTimings.description: Per-word or per-phrase timings from the actual audio when available. Phrase alignment is unreliable without these.

timingSource.description: measured_audio is the only value that licenses phrase-level automation. Anything else forces review of phrase-aligned events.

acceptableDurationSeconds.description: DESCRIPTIVE EXPECTATION, NOT A BUDGET. User ruling 2026-09-16: "time can be extended for this. we dont have to fit a duration if the video evidence needs 5 extra seconds to complete him saying the proof. we arent trying to cram or stretch to fit a duration budget." Corpus reference points: overall p25/median/p75 is 6.0/9.0/14.0s; infographic scenes sit near 16s. These describe what reference documentaries did. They never override the time the evidence needs to complete. Answer 14_scene_boundaries_and_visual_cadence says the same: derived ranges stay subordinate to claim communication, phrase alignment, readability and the needs of the passage.

minimumReadableHoldSeconds.description: Floor before any element may be replaced. Derived from 502 observed gaps between consecutive internal changes: p10 1.5s, p25 2.0s, median 3.0s, and only 0.6% of real gaps fall below 1.0s. Treat 1.0s as an absolute floor and 1.5s as the working floor. Dense evidence text needs more.

internalChangeBudget.description: A scene earns roughly 6 to 7 seconds per internal visual change in the reference corpus, flat across every duration bucket up to 30s. USE AS A SPLIT HINT, NOT A CAP. It does not apply while a unit is extended for evidence to complete, and it does not apply to continuous testimony or performance. Under the elastic duration policy a long scene with few changes is a signal to look, not an automatic split.

durationPolicy.description: How the unit's length is decided. Elastic by default.

mode.description: elastic means the evidence sets the length. fixed_by_container is only for a scene whose native structure genuinely cannot extend.

evidenceMustComplete.description: When true, the unit runs until the proof finishes. A quoted clip plays to the end of the decisive sentence; a document holds until the decisive line has been readable long enough. Truncating the proof to hit a target duration is a failure, not a trade.

narrationYields.description: True when the narration pauses so source audio can carry the proof. Extends the unit and pushes the rest of the film later, which is expected rather than a problem.

extensionSeconds.description: How far past the narration this unit runs.

takeaway.description: The single thing the viewer must leave with. Exactly one. If two are needed the unit must be split.

narrationJob.description: Normalized visual communication job. Derived from rhetoricalFunction, which is one of the two reliable controlled axes in the reference corpus.

rhetoricalFunction.description: Controlled vocabulary carried over unchanged from the reference analyses so back-tests stay comparable.

claims.description: Every factual assertion the picture must not contradict and, where the claim is evidentiary, must actively support.

claimClass.description: Normalized replacement for the reference corpus's claimType field, which contained 442 distinct free-text values across 628 units and cannot be used as a feature as recorded.

evidenceObligation.description: The strictest obligation governs the unit. Corpus behaviour: evidence passages are exact_source_required 60% of the time and never license decorative media. Decorative media appears as the strictest obligation only on transition (10%) and setup (3%) beats.

sourceCandidates.description: Known primary sources that would satisfy the obligation. USER RULING 2026-09-16 on the deferred answer 18: the source of every proof role is recorded here and carried into the production handoff. On-screen attribution is an editorial choice per scene, never a requirement, and attribution capability is never used to filter containers.

entities.description: Named people, organizations, works, places or objects that must be visible or identifiable.

mustBeNamedOnScreen.description: If true, the container must have a text slot. Several carousel packs on the drive have zero text slots and cannot satisfy this.

recognitionRisk.description: high means the viewer will not know who this is without a label.

focalEntityCount.description: Drives container capacity. Corpus: interview footage carries one entity 77% of the time; carousels carry one entity only 20% of the time and rise to 58% share at four entities; infographics are the only container reaching beyond four. Median unit duration rises 8.5s to 10.2s to 13.0s from one to three entities, then stops rising because four-plus entities are shown simultaneously rather than sequenced.

entityRelationship.description: Normalized replacement for the corpus's free-text entityRelationship field (580 distinct values in 628 units).

requiredMedia.description: Media ROLES, never filenames. This is the output of the narration stage and the input to retrieval. Filenames are bound later, in the candidate, never here.

editorialRole.description: Controlled vocabulary carried from the reference corpus, where it was one of only four reliable axes.

contentRequirement.description: What must actually be depicted, in plain language. 'The 1998 filing, page showing the dismissal clause' not 'a legal document'.

mediaFamily.description: Coarse family used for retrieval and for treatment scoring. Back-testing shows this field, not the narration structure, is what actually resolves treatment choice.

legibilityRequirement.description: Illegible evidence is the second most common failure mode in the reference corpus.

eraConstraint.description: Period the asset must belong to. Anachronistic footage for a historical claim is an explicit corpus failure mode ('using modern' appears 7 times in failure conditions).

fallbackAcceptable.description: What may substitute, and at what cost. Empty means nothing may substitute.

sourceRef.description: Where this role's evidence actually came from once bound. URL, archive reference, document name or asset path. Recorded for every proof role.

attributionPolicy.description: record_only: provenance is tracked in the contract and handoff; whether a credit appears in frame is decided per scene.

visualEvents.description: What the picture must DO, tied to the words that motivate it. 88.8% of reference events are rated strong alignment, so this is the field the whole system is judged on.

triggerPhrase.description: The exact spoken words that motivate this event. Must appear verbatim in narration.text.

triggerOffsetSeconds.description: Seconds from unit start. Corpus median for the FIRST event is 2.3s, and only 30% of units fire their first event within 1s of the cut. Scenes establish, then the event lands. Do not default to zero.

toleranceSeconds.description: How far the event may drift from the trigger before alignment is judged failed.

criticality.description: decisive events that cannot be aligned are a hard rejection of the candidate.

carryForward.description: Elements that should persist from the previous scene.

mustDifferFrom.description: Assets or treatments used recently that would read as a repeat.

bridgeRequired.description: True when the visual family changes and a transition must carry the change. A family change with a good bridge is allowed, not a defect.

prohibitions.description: What must never be shown or implied. Populated from the claim set: anything the narration does not support.

failureConditions.description: Corpus frequency of failure themes across 681 recorded conditions: generic or stock or unrelated stand-in 19 per 100, illegible text 8, timing miss 6, clutter 5, anachronism and monotony below that.

rulesetVersion.description: Version of the active rule set that produced this contract. Required for rollback.
